changes.why: CARD ADVANTAGE, ON TOP OF lands-v1 (this list carries its two fetches and the Swamp). deck-audit reads five draw copies against a target of ten. Skullclamp in: fifteen of the deck's infect bodies have one toughness, so every equip draws two, and it is the one activation docs/gotchas-bench.md shows Forge's AI actually uses (1.25 activations per cast, against 0.00 for Ashnod's Altar) -- the goldfish cannot read it and the record will. Read the Bones and Dark Confidant in as draw the goldfish CAN read. Out: Combat Celebrant and Staff of Compleation, the two cards the 55-card leave-one-out sweep ranked least needed among the non-interaction, both of whose real value is in an activation or an extra combat the model does not price; and Ogre Menial, a four-mana 3/3 the sweep found worth 0.001 of kill_by_8. Objective on the draw axis the goldfish sees; Skullclamp's share is Forge's to measure.

derived.name: THE OBJECTIVE
derived.what: One falsifiable threshold, written when the branch was OPENED and before anything was measured.
derived.why: It is the only thing here that can fail. Everything else is a description of what changed; this is the claim the branch made about itself, graded against its own minimum detectable difference.

derived.name: THE MANA
derived.what: Karsten's hypergeometric source targets against the pip distribution each list actually has, and the on-curve probability the base achieves.
derived.why: Deterministic, and the nine sampled rows cannot see it. A branch that changes its spells changes its pip distribution, so the target moves underneath the base — which is why the GAP is the figure and not the source count.

derived.name: MDE
derived.what: The minimum detectable difference: the smallest gap this many games could resolve at 95% confidence.
derived.why: A row marked `noise` is NOT a row where nothing happened. It is a row where whatever happened is smaller than this run can see, which rules out a large effect and says nothing about a small one.

derived.name: THE BILL
derived.what: Every card in the branch, sorted by where it physically is: already in the deck, in a box, in another deck, or not owned.
derived.why: The only cost figure in the report. `buy` is money; `elsewhere` is a card that has to come out of a deck that is currently sleeved.

board power @T6.what: Total power on the battlefield at the end of turn 6.
board power @T6.why: The deck's turn-6 threat, before any of it has connected. It is what a table sees and decides to answer, and it moves earlier than damage does.

damage @T10.scale: the opponent starts at 40 life, so 40.0 is exactly lethal once
damage @T10.what: Cumulative damage dealt to the single goldfish opponent by the end of turn 10, averaged over every game.
damage @T10.why: The headline output figure and the one a doubler moves. It has no ceiling, so unlike the kill rate it keeps separating two lists after both of them already win.

extra cards by T8.scale: against the 8 cards every deck draws for free by then
extra cards by T8.what: Cards drawn BEYOND the one-a-turn draw step, cumulative to the end of turn 8, averaged over every game. Counts only draw the model can price — a card's own ETB draw, an instant or sorcery that draws, an upkeep trigger, and a trigger that draws when other creatures or tokens enter. Activated, X-based, sacrifice-gated and death-triggered draw are NOT counted and the cards are named in the goldfish artifact.
extra cards by T8.why: "Vampires on board, nothing in hand, no way to rebuild" is the most-repeated line in this deck's log, and until 2026-08-28 the model could not see it: it drew one card a turn whatever the list said. Read it against the count of draw cards, not alone — a deck listing twelve draw sources whose modelled figure is one has almost no UNCONDITIONAL card advantage, and that is a fact about the deck rather than a limit of the parser.

hand can act by T3.scale: against the keep rate itself — this is a property of the seven cards kept, assuming no draws
hand can act by T3.what: The share of kept opening hands containing a nonland card the hand's own lands can pay for by turn three, counting at most three land drops and no draws.
hand can act by T3.why: A stricter threshold than the 2-5 lands rule the model actually mulligans by, and it is REPORTED rather than enforced, so it cannot restate a figure on any deck. It separates "this hand had lands" from "this hand could do something" — the distinction behind a two-land keep that never got going.

hoard @T10.what: Treasures sitting in the hoard at the end of turn 10, averaged over every game.
hoard @T10.why: The second axis, and the only one that is not combat. It is near-uncorrelated with damage, power and kill (r = 0.08-0.25 across the fleet), so it can fall while they rise and mean it. For this deck Treasures are incidental ramp, never an engine.

hoard @T6.what: The same count at the end of turn 6 — the hoard you actually have when the deck wants to deploy, rather than the one you end up with.
hoard @T6.why: A big turn-10 hoard that was not there on turn 6 arrived too late to cast anything that mattered.

interaction affordable @T6.scale: conditional on holding one — the denominator is games where an answer was in hand, not all games
interaction affordable @T6.what: Of the games where an answer was in hand on turn 6, the share where the turn also ended with enough unspent mana to cast it. The suite is removal + sweepers + protection, the same set `deck-audit` counts.
interaction affordable @T6.why: The pilot's own diagnosis of a lost game: "Deflecting Swat and Teferi's Protection sat in my hand uncast for the entire game ... my mana was spent casting vampires, so there was never open mana to hold up." This is that claim as a number. It is CONDITIONAL on purpose: the raw castable rate falls when you simply cut interaction, which answers a different question. Measured at the END OF THE MAIN PHASE, before combat is paid for. And it is a FLOOR — the model casts everything it can afford every turn, so a pilot choosing to hold up scores higher.

killed by T10.scale: a CLOCK against one unblocking opponent, never a win rate
killed by T10.what: The same, by the end of turn 10 — the harness's last turn.
killed by T10.why: Whether the deck closes at all. It saturates near 1.0, so on a list that already wins it stops discriminating and damage @T10 is the honest axis instead.

killed by T6.scale: a CLOCK against one unblocking opponent, never a win rate
killed by T6.what: The share of games in which cumulative damage reaches 40 by the end of turn 6.
killed by T6.why: THE CLOCK, at the turn a real pod is still setting up. This is the figure a faster list is bought for.

missed drop by T5.what: The share of games that miss at least one land drop across turns 1 to 5.
missed drop by T5.why: The single best predictor of a slow start, and the row most sensitive to a land count change.

mulliganed.what: The share of games that took at least one mulligan under the harness rule: keep a 7 with 2-5 lands, up to two redraws.
mulliganed.why: A proxy for whether the land count fits the curve. It should barely move unless the land count did.

stall, 2 in a row.what: The share of games with two consecutive turns, from turn 2 on, where nothing in hand could be cast with the mana available.
stall, 2 in a row.why: Two dead turns in a row is how a deck loses without ever being interacted with. Curve and colour problems both surface here.

forge.why: no Forge run on the deck — `manamap pilot simulate ingris-infect --vs <pod>` puts it at a table and writes where this reads

limits: The goldfish has no opponents and nothing blocks: its kill turn is a CLOCK, not a win rate, and it cannot see interaction, removal or any alternate win.
Nothing here reads `goldfish_targets.json`'s `required` flags. The engine lift did, and was deleted for it: the declaration is authored, so the same hand set the target and read the verdict.

Card advantage is measured only where the model can price it. Activated, X-based, sacrifice-gated and death-triggered draw are unmodelled and named per deck in `goldfish_metrics.json`; on a sacrifice-based list that is most of it.

Death-triggered DRAIN is not modelled at all — nothing dies in this simulation. Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat and Bastion of Remembrance contribute nothing to any damage or kill row here. A branch built on them is understated by however much that line is worth, and `simulate` against a real pod is the only place it can be measured.
